svg.title: Labora design system
svg.text: Colors, type, components, and rules for every Labora screen, post, and image.
The mark is an L that turns like a bench workflow, with a dot for the sample. Never redraw, stretch, or recolor it.
On white, cream, or mint backgrounds
On Deep Teal and dark photography
For small brand moments and stickers
Keep empty space around the logo equal to
half the height of the mark on every side.
Mark: 24 px tall. Full logo: 96 px wide.
Below that, use the mark alone.
A calm, nature-led palette: deep teal for authority, warm green for action, mint and cream for space.
About 60% neutral space, 30% Deep Teal, 10% Labora Green.
Green is the accent: one button, one highlight, or one icon set per layout.
Measured WCAG contrast. Normal text needs 4.5:1 (AA). Large, bold text needs 3:1.
Mulish for everything. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, never from extra colors or all caps.
Free on Google Fonts. Fallback: Segoe UI, Arial.
Bring samples, inventory, and equipment together.
Every record is attributable, traceable, and protected.
An 8-point rhythm, soft rounded corners, and two shadow levels only.
Section padding 96–128 px. Card padding 24 px.
Building blocks used across the site and product visuals. Reuse them in posts instead of inventing new ones.
Primary: one per view, Labora Green.
Secondary: ghost with a gray outline.
On dark: Bright Green fill, white outline.
Status pill, module tag, and eyebrow. Sentence case only.
Outline icons on a 24 px grid, 1.8 px stroke, rounded ends. Labora Green on a Mint tile.
Three layouts for LinkedIn and Instagram. Export at 1080 × 1080 px. Product UI is always the hero.
Cream background, Deep Teal headline, one green button.
Registration to report, in one record.
Deep Teal, white headline, Light Green icons, Bright Green CTA.
Mint background, module tag, a real product card.
Quick rules for designers and anyone making Labora images.
Lead with product UI and dashboards
Use one green accent per layout
Use real product screens or the mockup style above
Use stock lab photos as the main visual
Add blue, purple, or rainbow gradients
Put Bright or Light Green text on white
Stack many shadows, glows, or glass effects
Invent customer numbers, awards, or certifications
Font: Mulish (Google Fonts). Colors match the website stylesheet.
